label: copy-phase input p fed back at recall position >= 3
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the fed-back input token is p, i.e. the model just output p, and that p was original token index >= 2 (recall_idx >= 3). Never fires on p during the original phase, at the delimiter, or on any other token (one stray u). It is weak or absent when the fed-back p came from original position 0-1: rate 0 at recall_idx <= 1, small at recall_idx 2, about 3.3% of steps at recall_idx >= 3, which with the p rate is close to always. Magnitude grows with how late in the sequence the p sits: the lowest-quartile examples are p at original index 2, and the top examples are p at original index 4-7. Fires for repeated p too (consecutive p p both fire). Not modulated by the output token, previous tokens or first token.

issues: Minor boundary noise only. In the test split, 558 false positives (about 1% of predicted steps) are mostly at recall_idx 3, i.e. p at original index 2 in longer sequences. Precision at recall_idx==3 is 0.97. Restricting by L>=7 or to_go>=4 did not isolate a clean failing class, so this is a soft onset at the boundary, not a systematic gap.

The 1350 missed steps are tiny activations (0.01-0.09 of max) at recall_idx 2, i.e. p at original index 1. They hold 0.4% of activation mass. recall_idx==2 alone scores precision 0.08, so 'only weakly at recall_idx 2' is accurate. It would be more precise to say it fires there rarely (about 8% of the time) and faintly.

Checked claims. In the dev profile, all activation falls in the copy phase (none in the original phase or at the delimiter). in_tok p carries 1.000 of the mass, with one stray u. Mass per active step rises with recall_idx (recall 3: 0.137/15668 vs recall 5: 0.250/11119), which supports 'magnitude grows later'. Repeated p (prev_tok==p, precision 0.98), in_count>=2 (0.99) and out_tok==p (0.998) do not hurt precision, which supports 'output/previous tokens don't matter'.
Test-split scores are confirmed: P 0.990, R 0.977, F1 0.984, mass recall 0.996. Adding to_go<=5 gives F1 0.985 on dev, a negligible gain.
